prompt_text: My AC needs repair in Houston. Which specific HVAC companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Houston for AC repair?
answer_verbatim:
I can give better, tailored names if you tell me your Houston ZIP or neighborhood. If you want immediate options now, here are several reputable choices to call and why — plus what to ask them and red flags to watch for.

Recommended companies to call (Houston-wide)
- John Moore Services
  - Why: Houston-based, long-established, offers 24/7 emergency repairs, maintenance plans, and handles warranty work. Large enough to usually have same‑day availability.
- ARS/Rescue Rooter (Houston)
  - Why: National network with local crews; known for emergency service and a broad range of HVAC/plumbing services. Convenient if you want a company that handles both urgent fixes and replacements.
- Abacus Plumbing, AC & Electric
  - Why: Texas company with a strong Houston presence and good local reviews. Offers diagnostics, emergency service, and financing options.
- One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning (Houston franchise)
  - Why: Franchise promise of prompt arrival windows and service guarantees — useful when you need a quick repair.
- Your manufacturer’s authorized dealer (Carrier, Trane, Lennox, etc.)
  - Why: If your unit is under warranty, an authorized dealer can do covered repairs without voiding the warranty and has factory training for your brand.

What to tell them when you call
- Brief symptom summary (e.g., “compressor not starting,” “blowing warm air,” “no power to thermostat”), make/model if known, when problem began, and whether you have a warranty.
- Ask: Are your technicians NATE-certified? Do you offer flat-rate repair pricing or a diagnostic fee? Is emergency/same‑day service available? Does the repair come with a labor warranty and parts warranty? Do you install replacements of my brand and model?

Red flags and things to avoid
- No license or insurance information when asked.
- Extremely low quote over the phone with “we’ll see” onsite and then large surprise upsells.
- Pressure to replace a unit before showing diagnostic evidence (photos, clear test results).
- Refusal to provide a written estimate or warranty terms.

If you want, give your ZIP or the cross-streets and whether this is an emergency (no AC at all, heat wave, with infants/elderly), and I’ll look up 3–4 top-rated, nearby HVAC companies with phone numbers and recent review notes so you can call them now.
